questions.title: Most Days Above 90°F Per Year
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by average number of days per year with a maximum temperature at or above 90°F.
questions.disclaimer: Statewide averages derived from NOAA reporting stations. Desert Southwest and Gulf Coast dominate; Alaska and Hawaii have essentially zero. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: NOAA NCEI — Comparative Climatic Data, Mean Number of Days Maximum Temperature >= 90°F

questions.title: Most Days Below 32°F Per Year
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by average number of days per year with a minimum temperature at or below freezing (32°F).
questions.disclaimer: Statewide averages from NOAA station normals. Elevation and latitude drive rankings — some interior western states outrank their eastern peers of similar latitude. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: NOAA NCEI — Comparative Climatic Data, Mean Number of Days Minimum Temperature <= 32°F

questions.title: Most Lightning Strikes Per Square Mile
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by average annual cloud-to-ground lightning flash density (strikes per square mile).
questions.disclaimer: Flash density = cloud-to-ground lightning strikes per square mile per year, averaged across the state. Vaisala NLDN is the standard reference dataset used by NOAA/NWS. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Vaisala National Lightning Detection Network — Annual Lightning Report

questions.title: Most Severe Thunderstorm Days Per Year
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by average number of severe thunderstorm days per year (days with hail 1+ inch, wind 58+ mph, or a tornado report).
questions.disclaimer: A 'severe thunderstorm day' is any calendar day with at least one qualifying severe report in the state (hail >= 1 in, wind >= 58 mph, or tornado). Definition per NOAA SPC. Includes Washington DC.

questions.title: Most Cities Over 100,000 Population
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the number of incorporated cities with a population above 100,000.
questions.disclaimer: Counts only cities that are legally incorporated municipalities; CDPs (census-designated places) and unincorporated communities are excluded. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — City & Town Population Totals (Vintage 2023)

questions.title: Most Cities Over 500,000 Population
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the number of cities with a population above 500,000.
questions.disclaimer: Uses incorporated city (not metro area) population. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Top City Population Estimates (Vintage 2023)

questions.title: Largest City by Population
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the population of their single largest city.
questions.disclaimer: Uses each state's largest incorporated city (not metro area). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — City Population Estimates (Vintage 2023)

questions.title: Largest State Capital by Population
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the population of the state capital city.
questions.disclaimer: Ranks each state by the population of its designated capital city, not its largest city. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — City Population Estimates (Vintage 2023)

questions.title: Highest Urban Population Share
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the percentage of population living in urban areas.
questions.disclaimer: Uses the Census Bureau's 2020 definition of urban areas (≥5,000 people or ≥2,000 housing units in a contiguous developed area). Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — 2020 Census Urban and Rural Classification

questions.title: Lowest Urban Population Share
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the LOWEST percentage of population living in urban areas (most rural first).
questions.disclaimer: Rank 1 = the MOST rural state. Uses the Census 2020 urban-area definition. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — 2020 Census Urban and Rural Classification

questions.title: Tallest Building
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the height of their single tallest completed building (roof/architectural height).
questions.disclaimer: Uses architectural height (top of spire/roof) per CTBUH, not antenna height. Only completed buildings — under-construction towers excluded. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat (CTBUH) — Tallest Building Database

answers.value: 422 ft (Wells Fargo Center, Salt Lake City)

questions.title: Most Fortune 500 HQ Cities
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the total number of Fortune 500 company headquarters located in them.
questions.disclaimer: Counts total F500 HQs in the state, not the number of distinct cities that host one. Includes Washington DC.

questions.title: Most Amtrak Stations
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the number of Amtrak passenger rail stations.
questions.disclaimer: Counts all active Amtrak-served stations, including thruway bus-only connections at some stops. Includes Washington DC.

questions.title: Largest Metropolitan Area
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the population of their largest Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA).
questions.disclaimer: Uses the Census-defined MSA (not CSA / combined). MSAs that cross state lines are credited to the state containing the principal city. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Metropolitan Statistical Area Population Estimates

questions.title: Most Cities in the Top 100 by Population
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the number of cities in the US top 100 most populous.
questions.disclaimer: Only incorporated cities are counted; CDPs excluded. Ties broken alphabetically for consecutive ranks. Includes Washington DC.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Top 100 US Cities (Vintage 2023)

questions.title: Most Colleges in a Single City
questions.prompt: Rank the US states by the number of degree-granting colleges/universities in their most college-dense city.
questions.disclaimer: Counts Title IV degree-granting institutions in a single principal city (not the whole metro). Boston's total is inflated by many small specialty and religious institutions. Includes Washington DC.
